deliverables: Upgrade Cardano mainnet protocol to major version 11 and minor version 0 while remaining in the Conway era.
Make new Plutus primitives available as defined in CIP-0109, CIP-0132, CIP-0133, CIP-0138 and CIP-0153.
Make all Plutus built-in functions available consistently across Plutus V1, V2 and V3.
Add UPLC case expressions for Bool, Integer and Data.
Enforce or tighten several ledger and node validation, diagnostic, and security rules.
request.what: Initiate a hard fork upgrading Cardano Mainnet to protocol version 11.0, called the 'van Rossem' hard fork.

claims.claim: The hard fork will upgrade Cardano Mainnet from protocol version 10.0 to protocol version 11.0 while remaining in the Conway era and not changing transaction shape.

The upgrade introduces new Plutus primitives for modular exponentiation, dropList, BLS12-381 multi-scalar multiplication, Array operations, and native Value handling, with the referenced CIPs identifying the primitives.
The proposal states that all Plutus built-ins, including newly introduced ones, will become available across Plutus V1, V2 and V3.
The proposal claims native UPLC case expressions over Bool, Integer and Data will improve performance and produce cleaner script logic.

The proposal claims the upgrade tightens ledger and node behavior by enforcing VRF key hash uniqueness, revising Plutus V1/V2 reference input rules, promoting Constitutional Committee voting restrictions to ledger predicates, rewriting withdrawal validation, and improving PPView mismatch diagnostics.

The proposal states that testing reports demonstrate no behavioral regressions, complete conformance between specification and implementation for new ledger rules, and correct operation of new Plutus features across V1, V2 and V3.

The proposal links a Cardano Node 11.0.1 performance report and says it shows no regressions for standard value, Plutus, and voting benchmarks, plus acceptable baseline performance for new Plutus primitives and case expressions.
The proposal states that security audits have been undertaken for Plutus BLS primitives and execution costs for all Plutus primitives.

The proposal says at least 85% of stake pools by active stake should have upgraded to a node version capable of protocol version 11 before ratification, and that this must be verified before ratification.

The proposal states that reversion is only possible in extreme circumstances through the CIP-0135 disaster recovery process, while Plutus primitive usage could be disabled through companion cost model settings if issues are discovered.

summary: The document proposes a no-treasury hard fork to Cardano protocol version 11.0 with Plutus, ledger, node diagnostic, and security changes, supported by references to CIPs and a performance report but with several readiness, testing, audit, and risk details asserted rather than fully evidenced in the anchor text.
